title: CHEAR: Confusion-Hierarchy Evidence-Aware Reasoning for Cost-Efficient Human Activity Recognition

claim.summary: CHEAR builds an activity-confusion hierarchy and activity-pair feature knowledge offline from source-domain retrieval errors, then has an LLM retain variable-size candidate sets level by level and read pairwise feature reports only for surviving pairs before choosing an activity label.

modules.name: Confusion-hierarchy variable-size candidate retention
modules.scope_reason: Groups are built from directed confusions among activity labels and the LLM prunes label candidates level by level, so the workflow is tied to the classification label space.
evidence_locators: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Inference starts from root candidate"
PDF p.4; passage beginning "Meaning of the activity-confusion hierarchy."

modules.name: On-demand activity-pair feature knowledge
modules.scope_reason: Feature knowledge is registered for confusable activity pairs and can only favour one of its two label endpoints, so it is bound to the classification output.
